function: Channel estimation: GNNs refine initially estimated channels from two adjacent subcarriers to the true channel matrices, exploiting spatial-frequency correlation (pp. 3-4).
system: Downlink mmWave massive MIMO-OFDM, hybrid architecture: N=32 transmit and NR=32 receive antennas, 2 RF chains each, K=64 subcarriers, 28 GHz carrier; no RIS (pp. 3, 11).
method: Spatial-frequency GNNs (SF-GNN-T, SF-GNN-R, SF-GNN-TR) with MLP aggregation and combination layers, supervised offline training with MSE loss, Adam; trained on small arrays and applied without retraining (pp. 5-11).
data_channel: 3GPP TR 38.901 Release 15 channel model [44]: 6000 training, 1000 testing, 1000 validation channel samples; L=3 paths, K=64 subcarriers, 28 GHz, 100 MHz sampling rate (p. 11).
test_conditions: Trained at N=NR=32, K=64, L=3, SNR 5-15 dB; tested at other SNRs, L=1-4, N or NR up to 512 without retraining, and under pilot contamination (pp. 11-14).
baselines: Non-learned: LS, LMMSE. Learned: SF-CNN [27], MLP, GNN of conference version [1]; ablation GNN-T (pp. 11-12).
metrics: NMSE versus SNR, training epochs, number of antennas, number of main paths and pilot contamination (pp. 10-14).
complexity: FLOPs-based orders: SF-GNN-T (Eq. 35), SF-GNN-TR (Eq. 36), versus LMMSE O((N N_R)^3) and SF-CNN; no numeric FLOPs or measured runtime (pp. 10-11).
q1_support: p. 11: "the 3GPP TR 38.901 Release 15 channel model" is the stated source of the 6000, 1000 and 1000 channel samples used for training, testing and validation.
q2_support: p. 13: "first train the SF-GNN-T under the setting with N = 32. We then" test up to N = 512 without retraining; p. 13: "paths to test the trained SF-GNN-T and SF-GNN-R by using the" 1000 samples with L = 1 to 4 after training at L = 3.
q3_support: p. 11: "SF-CNN [27] and MLP) and conventional channel estimation schemes (i.e., LS and LMMSE)" are the baselines; Fig. 7 compares them with the SF-GNNs in NMSE, and the GNN of [1] is the authors' earlier learned estimator.
q4_support: p. 10: "approaches by utilizing the number of floating point operations" (FLOPs) gives the complexity orders of the SF-GNNs (Eqs. 35, 36), compared with LMMSE O((N N_R)^3) and SF-CNN; no numeric FLOPs or runtime.
q5_support: p. 11: "generate 6000, 1000, and 1000 channel samples as the training" set, testing set and validation set; the samples are generated by the authors, with no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Area 2: channel estimation, evaluated in NMSE. q1: the text cites [44] for 3GPP TR 38.901, but the reference list gives the 3GPP report as [45] and [44] as another work; the channel is written as a generic L-path geometric model in Eqs. 1-4 and the TR 38.901 scenario is not specified, reviewer to confirm. q3: SF-CNN [27], MLP and the GNN of the conference version [1] are counted as learned baselines; GNN-T is an ablation and is not counted. q4: only FLOPs orders are given.
